contexts.text: Those not so innocent (as the naked) appear in garments... as of diamond-like silk.
Its lower spiritual and doctrinal things are garments of silk, etc. AC 5319:2. AC 5620:4.
Fine linen and silk () = truths from good; but these [fabrics] in Heaven, being in its light, are resplendent and transparent.
To make flax of silk () = to feign truths. ( = spiritual truth. AE 654:50.)
Silk, etc. () = celestial goods and truths.
The prince wore a tunic of shining silk of a hyacinthine colour.
They wore robes and tunics of refulgent silk, in which were inwoven flowers...
Some with hats bound with silk, who were of the ecclesiastical order.
Mary appeared in white raiment as of silk.
The African women appear in striped garments of silk (the men in the like of linen).
Fine linen and silk = truths from a celestial origin. AE 1143:2.
Fine linen = genuine truth; silk = the same resplendent from interior good.
Silk = truth from a spiritual origin. AE 1144. AE 1144:2, Explained.
Spiritual Angels (wear) fine linen and silk.
